audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this matchup appears nowhere on the page: Steadfast Presence (W) stops Noxian Guillotine. Every mention of R treats it as an unstoppable execute.
audit.why: Riot's text on Poppy W: "Poppy can activate Steadfast Presence to gain Move Speed and stop enemy dashes around her. If a dash is stopped, the enemy is slowed and grounded." Riot's text on Darius R: "Darius leaps to an enemy champion" — the kit file carries the dash flag on it for exactly this reason. A Darius who presses R into an active W loses a 120s cooldown for nothing and is then slowed and grounded on top of her. W is 20s at rank 1 falling to 12s at rank 5, so it is baitable, but only if the player knows to bait it.
audit.corrected: Stated in spikes[1], phases[4].why, whys[4], mid, dontsFull[2].d, report[5], report[11], wants.foe[1] and the cooldown breakdown: bait the 12-20s W, then press R.
sources: champ-data/_kits darius R text + dash flag

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and content.mid both say Keeper's Verdict "can cancel your E Apprehend charge". Apprehend has no charge — it is an instant 535-range cone sweep.
audit.why: Riot's text: "When activated, Darius sweeps up his enemies with his axe's hook and pulls them to him." There is no wind-up to interrupt. The real relationship runs the other way: Keeper's Verdict is the channel (channel flag: interruptible), and Apprehend's displacement breaks it.
audit.corrected: Both strings rewritten. tldr, report[0] and dontsFull[1].d now tell the player to Apprehend her out of the Verdict channel instead.
sources: champ-data/_kits poppy R text + channel flag

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.early says "her W shields/grounds". Steadfast Presence does not shield. Poppy's only shield is Iron Ambassador (passive), from picking her thrown buckler back up.
audit.why: Riot's text on the passive: "Poppy throws her buckler that bounces off the target. Poppy can pick it up to gain a temporary shield." W's text gives Armor, Magic Resist that scale up as she drops low, Move Speed, and dash-stopping — no shield. Attributing the shield to W hides the one thing Darius can actually do about it: stand on the buckler so she cannot collect it.
audit.corrected: breakdown.early, phases[0].why and report[11] now name Iron Ambassador as the shield and tell the player to stomp the buckler.
sources: champ-data/_kits poppy P and W text

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] describes Hammer Shock as if it were a threat to be traded through, and nothing states that Poppy's W passive resists rise as her health falls — which is what makes a long Darius trade go worse the closer she is to dying.
audit.why: Riot's text: Q "creating a zone that will slow enemies and explode after a delay" — it is avoidable by walking out. W passive: "Poppy passively gains Armor and Magic Resist. This bonus increases when she is low on Health." That is a direct counter to Darius's physical-damage bleed pattern, and the answer in his own kit is Apprehend's passive armour shred plus the true damage on R.
audit.corrected: spikes[0], dosFull[2].d and breakdown.early restated around the resist ramp and the armour shred.
sources: champ-data/_kits poppy Q and W text
champ-data/_kits darius E text (armour shred), R trueDamage flag

audit.whatIsWrong: The 2+ items row says Darius (win[6]=Darius, phases[6].side=Darius, 6/10) while whys[6] on the same row says "Poppy scales into a durable teamfight disruptor who out-values your solo pressure", spikes[3] says "Poppy out-scales you as a tank", content.late says "Poppy's tank scaling flips it", and the packet levelChart's seventh entry is Poppy.
audit.why: Four independent strings and the packet all say Poppy owns the late game; only the side token disagreed. Her W passive resists compound with tank items and Steadfast Presence anchors teamfights, while Darius's solo pressure decays against grouped play.
audit.corrected: Level chart flipped as one group on row 6 only: win[6] and phases[6].side Darius -> Poppy, phases[6].rating 6/10 -> 4/10, and phases[6].why rewritten to state why. Final chart: Darius, Darius, Skill, Darius, Skill, Darius, Poppy — matching the packet's first six Darius entries and its Poppy seventh.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why leaks a raw formula into the page: "Noxian Guillotine deals true damage R = d + a \times Stacks, bypassing defensive items completely."
audit.why: That is unrendered LaTeX shown to a player mid-loading-screen. It is also the wrong claim to lead with here, since the level-6 story against Poppy is that both ults exist and hers denies yours.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to state the true-damage-vs-resists point in plain words and add the W and R denials, which is also what earns the "Skill" side token on that row.

audit.whatIsWrong: The trading rules never mention walls, which is the only thing that turns Heroic Charge from a shove into a stun.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Poppy dashes to the target and pushes it back. If the target is pushed into a wall, it is stunned." In open lane, E is a 10-14s ability that just displaces Darius — often toward his own side. Standing next to the lane wall is what makes it a kill setup.
audit.corrected: tradeGood, report[3], dosFull[0].d, report[5], report[9] and report[11] now key the trade rules to wall position rather than a vague "dodge it".

audit.why: diffRating 7/10 with a 52.16% Darius win rate over 1714 games is a fair read: Darius edges the lane but Poppy's resist scaling, dash-denial and wall-stun make it genuinely awkward. Left unchanged.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carries no numbers and a placeholder Ghost entry, and it tells the player to save Apprehend to "interrupt their dash trajectories mid-flight" — Apprehend does not stop dashes.
audit.why: The three cooldowns that actually decide this lane are Heroic Charge (10-14s), Steadfast Presence (12-20s) and Apprehend (16-26s). Those numbers turn 'bait it' into a countable window.
audit.corrected: Replaced with all three, each with its rank range and the specific thing it decides.
sources: champ-data/_kits poppy E and W cds

audit.whatIsWrong: Poppy is referred to as "he"/"him"/"his" in tradeGood, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[0].d, report[3], report[9], report[11] and the wave breakdowns.
audit.why: Poppy is female. Wrong pronouns undercut trust in the mechanics printed beside them.
audit.corrected: Fixed in every string this proposal rewrites; the remainder are listed in notes.

notes: Kit-flag misfires I did NOT assert on the page, per the rule that Riot's description outranks a derived flag: Poppy's Q carries a 'grounding' flag but Riot's text for Hammer Shock says only "creating a zone that will slow enemies and explode after a delay" — no grounding, so I wrote it as slow-only. Poppy's R carries 'untargetable' and 'grounding' flags but Riot's one-line text is "Poppy channels a hammer strike that knocks enemies very far away" — I asserted only the channel and the displacement. Darius's E carries a 'knockup' flag; Riot's text says he "pulls them to him", so I wrote pull/displacement, never knockup. Level chart flipped as one group on row 6 only. Remaining Poppy pronoun errors not covered here (no content change available to justify the edit): full.breakdown.mid ("wait for his Heroic Charge mistake"), full.breakdown.wave and full.report[4].t ("shoved to his tower"), full.dontsFull[0].d ("removes half his win condition") — worth a champion-level sweep. Also flagging without editing: full.breakdown.wave / report[4].t is 530 characters of padded prose that says one thing (freeze outside your turret); it is the worst-written string on this page and would be better rewritten wholesale than trimmed inside a 10% band. full.breakdown.difficulty duplicates full.report[14].t verbatim, unlike every other matchup where difficulty is its own sentence.
